glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Good morning'. A greeting used in the morning.
glossary.example: Maakye, agya! — Good morning, father!

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Good afternoon'. A greeting used in the afternoon.
glossary.example: Mahaha, ɔkyerɛkyerɛni! — Good afternoon, teacher!

glossary.definition: A polite Akan phrase meaning 'I greet you' or 'I bid you good day'.
glossary.example: Mema wo akye, ɔbaa — I greet you, madam.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Thank you'.
glossary.example: Medaase, me wura. — Thank you, sir.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Yes'.
glossary.example: Aane, mɛkɔ. — Yes, I will go.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'No'.
glossary.example: Daabi, menntumi. — No, I cannot.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'water'.
glossary.example: Mepe nsu — I want water.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'house' or 'room'.
glossary.example: Me dan no so — My house is big.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'government'.
glossary.example: Aban no boa nnipa — The government helps people.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'nation' or 'country'.
glossary.example: Ghana yɛ oman — Ghana is a nation.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'family' or 'clan'.
glossary.example: Me abusua yɛ kɛse — My family is large.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for God the Supreme Being.
glossary.example: Yeda Onyankopɔn ase — We thank God.

glossary.definition: An Akan expression meaning 'Help me', often said when greeting someone who is busy or working.
glossary.example: Madwoa, wo abɛyɛ adwuma? — Help me, have you finished working?

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Welcome'. Used to welcome a visitor.
glossary.example: Akwaaba, ɔhene! — Welcome, chief!

glossary.definition: An Akan farewell phrase meaning 'Go well' or 'Goodbye'.
glossary.example: Nante yie, maakye nka wo! — Go well, may morning meet you!

glossary.definition: An Akan phrase meaning 'How are you?' used to ask about someone's well-being.
glossary.example: Mi wo ho te sɛn, ɔna? — How are you, mother?

glossary.definition: A polite Akan phrase meaning 'Please' or 'I beg you'. Used to make requests.
glossary.example: Mepa wo kyew, ma me nsu. — Please, give me water.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Good' or 'Fine'. Often used as a response to greetings.
glossary.example: Eye, medaase. — It is good, thank you.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Useful' or 'Good for you'. Used to express that something benefits someone.
glossary.example: Ɛyɛ yo — It is good for you.

glossary.definition: The Akan negative command meaning 'Don't do'. Used to tell someone not to do something.
glossary.example: Nnyɛ saa — Don't do that.

glossary.definition: The Akan number word for 'One'.
glossary.example: Obaako bɛɛ — One person came.

glossary.definition: The Akan number word for 'Two'.
glossary.example: Mmienu nkoa — Two boys.

glossary.definition: The Akan number word for 'Three'.
glossary.example: Mmiɛnsa mmara — Three dollars.

glossary.definition: The Akan first-person singular pronoun meaning 'I' or 'Me'.
glossary.example: Me din yɛ Kofi — My name is Kofi.

glossary.definition: The Akan second-person pronoun meaning 'You' (singular). Can also mean 'Your'.
glossary.example: Wo din deɛn? — What is your name?

glossary.definition: The Akan third-person singular pronoun meaning 'He' or 'She'.
glossary.example: Ɔn yɛ ɔkyerɛkyerɛni — He/She is a teacher.

glossary.definition: The Akan first-person plural pronoun meaning 'We' or 'Us'.
glossary.example: Yɛn nyinaa bɛkɔ — All of us will go.

glossary.definition: The Akan second-person plural pronoun meaning 'You' (plural). Used when addressing more than one person.
glossary.example: Mo bɛkɔ ha? — Are you all coming here?

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Earth', 'Ground', or 'Land'.
glossary.example: Asaase no yɛ fertɛ — The land is fertile.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Woman' or 'Girl'.
glossary.example: Ɔbaa no yɛ fɛ — The woman is beautiful.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Man' or 'Boy'.
glossary.example: Ɔbarima no yɛ agya — The man is a father.

glossary.definition: A popular Ghanaian food made from pounded cassava and plantain, common in Akan households.
glossary.example: Medi fufu ne nkrakrana — I am eating fufu with soup.

glossary.definition: A Ghanaian food made from fermented corn and cassava dough, cooked into a smooth dough.
glossary.example: Banku ne tilapia yɛ dɛ — Banku with tilapia is delicious.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Forehead', a part of the body.
glossary.example: Me tan no esɔre — My forehead is sweating.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Hand', a part of the body.
glossary.example: Me nsa mu ama me — It is in my hands.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Good' or 'Well'. Used as an adjective to describe something positively.
glossary.example: Ɛyɛ pa — It is good.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Citizens' or 'People of a nation'.
glossary.example: Ɔmanfoɔ no bɛɛ — The citizens came.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Chiefs' or 'Rulers'. Plural of 'Ohene' (chief).
glossary.example: Ahemfoɔ no akɔbɔ amammerɛ mu — The chiefs have entered the palace.

glossary.definition: An Akan term for a 'Company' or 'Group' of people, especially traditional military companies in a town.
glossary.example: Asafoɔ no hyɛɛ ahoɔfa mu — The company gathered together.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Household' or 'Dwelling place'.
glossary.example: Me aguadi yɛ fam — My household is at home.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Mother'. An affectionate term for one's mother.
glossary.example: Mammy, me pe aduane — Mother, I want food.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Father'. An affectionate term for one's father.
glossary.example: Papa, meda wo ase — Father, I greet you.

glossary.definition: The Akan word for 'Festival' or 'Celebration'. A cultural event held by a community.
glossary.example: Asɔre no bɛba ɔsrane — The festival will come soon.

glossary.definition: A sacred day celebrated by the Akan people every 42 days (six weeks). It honours ancestors and the living chief.
glossary.example: Akwasidae yɛ nnɛ — Today is Akwasidae.

glossary.definition: A harvest festival celebrated by the Ga people of Ghana, meaning 'hooting at hunger' to remember a past famine.
glossary.example: Homowo yɛ Ga asafoɔ — Homowo is a Ga festival.

glossary.definition: An Akan purification and cleansing festival, especially associated with the Ashanti people.
glossary.example: Odwira yɛ ɔman mfonommu — Odwira is a national cleansing.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Big' or 'Large'.
glossary.example: Dan no yɛ kɛse — The house is big.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Beautiful' or 'Pretty'.
glossary.example: Ɔbaa no yɛ fɛ — The woman is beautiful.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Small' or 'Short'.
glossary.example: Abɔfra no yɛ kotte — The child is small.

glossary.definition: The Akan word meaning 'Now'. Refers to the present time.
glossary.example: Bra ha ɛnɛ — Come here now.
